how: A server of the bench's own answered www.example.com, mapped to 127.0.0.1 with --host-resolver-rules, on ports of five digits, over TLS 1.3 it speaks itself so that it gives ALPS (application_settings), which no Go TLS library gives: TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, X25519 and an ECDSA certificate taken on trust by --ignore-certificate-errors. For h2 it gave what each scenario names, and kept of each connection the code point and protocols of the ClientHello's ALPS, the settings the client's EncryptedExtensions gave, what each record of the client's encrypted handshake carried, the client's first SETTINGS frame and any GOAWAY, and the header block of every request as the bytes said it. Each scenario ran in a fresh profile: the run page opened from the command line, its script calling fetch() of /done/ID; a scenario of what a browser may refuse ran four seconds.
